# Run comparison view in the Dashboard (side-by-side and diff)

## Description

Delivers the core experiment-comparison capability in the Dashboard console. Users select two or more runs from the runs list and view their parameters and metrics side by side; for two selected runs, a diff view highlights which parameters and metrics changed. The comparison covers training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs as they are surfaced in the Dashboard, giving data scientists side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate runs and how their metrics differ, without exporting to spreadsheets.

## Scope

- Multi-select of two or more runs from the existing runs list in the Dashboard, opening a comparison that renders each selected run's parameters and metrics side by side (HLR-1).
- A diff mode for two selected runs that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between them, with changed values distinguishable from unchanged ones (HLR-3). This is delivered as a mode of the same comparison view: HLR-1 and HLR-3 are overlapping requirements (consolidated from two customer councils) that share the run-selection flow, the run parameter/metric data, and the Dashboard comparison surface.
- The comparison operates on runs within a single project; cross-project and cross-cluster comparison are out of scope per the strategy, as is automatic best-run selection or promotion.
- Data Science Pipelines requires no code changes for this capability: run parameters and metrics already surface on per-run pages and pipeline runs are surfaced in the Dashboard. Pipeline runs are comparison subjects, and existing per-run behavior must keep working — captured as acceptance criteria below rather than as separate pipeline work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the runs list in the Dashboard, when a user selects two or more runs, then a comparison opens showing each selected run's parameters and metrics side by side.
- Given a comparison of two selected runs, when the diff view is opened, then the parameters and metrics whose values differ between the two runs are highlighted, and unchanged values remain distinguishable.
- Given a selection that includes both training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs, then all selected runs render in the same comparison with their parameters and metrics.
- Given the comparison capability is in use, then existing per-run pages for pipeline runs continue to function unchanged (no regression to Data Science Pipelines run pages).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): "Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard" — fully covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P1): "Provide a run 'diff' view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs" — covered by the diff mode of this epic. HLR-1 and HLR-3 overlap in wording and substance (the strategy notes requirements were consolidated from two customer councils with kept overlap); both describe the same Dashboard comparison surface and share the run-selection flow and parameter/metric data, so they are implemented together rather than as two epics building the same surface independently.

# Run lineage on registered model versions

## Description

Registered model versions record a reference to the run that produced them, so the lineage from a registered model version back to its producing run is stored in the Model Registry and resolvable by consumers. This establishes the data foundation for opening a run comparison from the Model Registry and for making model promotion decisions with visibility into the experiments behind each candidate.

## Scope

- A registered model version carries a reference to the run that produced it, recorded through the registration flow and stored via the Model Registry's documented extension point for structured metadata on model versions (custom properties), per the Model Registry architecture context — no changes to the RegisteredModel / ModelVersion / ModelArtifact entity schemas.
- The lineage reference is retrievable through the Model Registry REST API alongside existing model version metadata, and uniquely identifies the producing run within its project.
- The linkage is additive metadata: model versions registered without run information register exactly as before, with no lineage reference.
- Dashboard-side surfacing of the lineage (showing the producing run and opening a comparison from the registry UI) is out of this epic's scope; that is Dashboard-owned work building on the linkage defined here.
- The linkage format is validated with a minimal stub — a model version carrying a synthetic run reference, created and read back through the API — not by building any user-facing surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a model version registered from a run, then the version's metadata identifies the run that produced it, and the reference is retrievable through the Model Registry REST API.
- Given a model version registered without run information, then registration succeeds and the version carries no lineage reference (existing registration behavior unchanged).
- Given the lineage reference on a model version, then it resolves to a single identifiable run within the project whose parameters and metrics are reachable through existing per-run data.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): "Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" — the link-back half of this requirement is covered by this epic; the registry-UI half (a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry) is covered by the Dashboard-owned registry entry-point work.

# Open run comparison from the Model Registry

## Description

In the Model Registry UI (surfaced in the Dashboard console), users can see the run that produced a registered model version and open the run comparison seeded with that run. This connects registry browsing directly to experiment comparison, so model promotion decisions can be made with side-by-side visibility into the runs behind each candidate.

## Scope

- The registry UI in the Dashboard shows the producing run on a registered model version, using the run lineage recorded in the Model Registry.
- An entry point on the model version (action or link) opens the run comparison seeded with the producing run, from which further runs can be added to the comparison.
- This epic adds the registry-side entry point only. The comparison view itself — multi-run selection, side-by-side rendering of parameters and metrics, and the diff mode — is the Dashboard runs-list comparison capability and is not rebuilt here.
- Cross-project and cross-cluster comparison remain out of scope per the strategy; the entry point operates within the model version's project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a registered model version that carries run lineage, when viewing it in the Model Registry UI, then the producing run is visible and an action opens the run comparison seeded with that run.
- Given a model version without recorded run lineage, then its registry view renders normally, without the comparison entry point.
- Given a comparison opened from the Model Registry, then it presents the same side-by-side and diff behavior as a comparison started from the runs list, and further runs can be added to it.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P1): "Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry" — the registry-UI half of this requirement is covered by this epic, building on the run-lineage metadata stored in the Model Registry and on the Dashboard's run comparison capability.
